title: Affine K-injective counit compatibility
statement: For $f,P,R,a,I,n$ as in [def-sc-affine-algebra-counit-homology-comparison], the homology of the termwise counit factors through the specified canonical mate: $H^n(\epsilon_I)=\epsilon_{H^n(I)}\circ P(m_{I,n})\circ c_{RI}$. No K-injectivity or quasi-coherence assumption is needed for this identity.

proof.text: By the definition of the mate, the inverse adjunction bijection sends it to c inverse followed by homology of the counit. Use Adjunction.homEquiv_symm_apply and Equiv.symm_apply_apply, then cancel c.hom against c.inv.

proof_origin.place: homEquiv_symm_apply and Equiv.symm_apply_apply; G1 canonical-mate repair

mathlib_searches.query: homology comparison for affine direct image of K-injective complexes and the pullback pushforward counit

lean.statement:
theorem affine_algebra_kinjective_counit_compatibility
    {X Y : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    (P : SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings (directImageAlgebraSpace f)) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    [P.Additive] [Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits P] [Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits P]
    (a : P ⊣ RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage (toDirectImageAlgebraSpace f))
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (n : ℤ) :
    HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((a.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).counit.app I) n =
      (P.mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso (.up ℤ) n).hom.app
        (((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage
          (toDirectImageAlgebraSpace f)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I) ≫
        P.map (affineAlgebraCounitHomologyComparison f P a I n) ≫
          a.counit.app (I.homology n)

statement_change.old_statement: Under the affine cohomology comparison e, the homology of the termwise counit of any additive exact left adjoint P equals the exact-functor homology comparison followed by P.map e and the ordinary counit.
statement_change.what: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the original quantified over every isomorphism e. For f=id on Spec(Q), P the identity and a nonzero quasi-coherent injective complex concentrated in degree zero, replacing the canonical e by -e negates the right-hand side while leaving the nonzero identity counit fixed. Replace arbitrary e by the explicitly constructed adjoint mate. Invertibility is a separate sourced theorem; the downstream existential statement is unchanged.
